collection: NCEE National Values Education: work and resolving conflict
note: Original four-option practice for final-year primary learners. ICPC historical teaching guidance is provisional. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Analyse causes of group disagreements and choose fair ways to resolve them.
questions.prompt: The sports club and drama club both need the hall after school. Each booked through a different teacher who could only see their own list. Which change would most directly prevent another clash?
questions.answer: Use one booking list both teachers can check before confirming a slot.
options: Use one booking list both teachers can check before confirming a slot.
Give the hall to the club that arrives first each day.
Ask one club to cancel all future bookings.
Put the two existing lists on opposite doors of the hall.
questions.explanation: A shared list lets both teachers notice a clash before either group is promised the hall.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Analyse causes of group disagreements and choose fair ways to resolve them.
questions.prompt: During a planning meeting, a team leader hears a complaint against a pupil who has gone to fetch supplies. What should the leader do before deciding what happened?
questions.answer: Ask the team to vote while the pupil is away.
options: Hear the pupil’s account and compare it with the available evidence.
Ask the team to vote while the pupil is away.
Tell the pupil to apologise as soon as they return.
Give the decision to whichever group has more members.
questions.explanation: Hearing both accounts and checking evidence allows a fair decision before anyone is blamed.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Analyse causes of group disagreements and choose fair ways to resolve them.
questions.prompt: Two exhibition teams argue over one display board. One needs to pin up work on Thursday to take photographs, while the other needs it all day on Friday for visitors. Which solution meets both needs?
questions.answer: Give each team half of the Friday session only.
options: Choose which team deserves the board by tossing a coin.
Schedule Thursday for photographs and Friday for the public display.
Give each team half of the Friday session only.
Ask both teams to arrive early on Friday and decide then.
questions.explanation: Their actual needs are on different days. A time-sharing agreement meets both without cancelling either activity.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Analyse causes of group disagreements and choose fair ways to resolve them.
questions.prompt: A pupil shares a message saying that one group deliberately took the other group’s paint. The art monitor discovers that the labels were accidentally switched. What should the pupil who shared the message do?
questions.answer: Delete their copy and let the other pupils draw their own conclusions.
options: Send the teacher a private message and keep repeating the first claim to friends.
Ask the art monitor to punish both groups equally.
Correct the message with the people who received it and explain what the monitor found.
Delete their copy and let the other pupils draw their own conclusions.
questions.explanation: Correcting the claim with the same audience can prevent blame from growing into a dispute and makes the evidence clear.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Apply responsibility and honesty in making and selling goods.
questions.prompt: A shoe maker in Aba notices that a row of stitching is coming loose before a customer collects a new pair of sandals. Which response shows care for the customer and pride in the work?
questions.answer: Repair the seam, check it and tell the customer if collection will be delayed.
options: Repair the seam, check it and tell the customer if collection will be delayed.
Cover the loose thread with polish and keep the collection time.
Ask the customer to pay extra for correcting the fault.
Leave the seam for the customer to discover after wearing the sandals.
questions.explanation: Checking and correcting workmanship protects the customer. Giving accurate notice of a delay respects their time.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Apply responsibility and honesty in making and selling goods.
questions.prompt: During furniture training, a learner copies a joint that works once but breaks when used again. Which action would most help the learner improve the quality of later work?
questions.answer: Use the same joint on every piece because it once worked.
options: Ask the trainer to explain what failed, then practise and test a corrected joint.
Use the same joint on every piece because it once worked.
Tell other learners to stop making the joint.
Choose a different piece of furniture without finding out why the joint broke.
questions.explanation: Feedback followed by practice and testing helps the learner identify and correct the underlying problem.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Apply responsibility and honesty in making and selling goods.
questions.prompt: A shop advertises stools as made by a nearby workshop. The next delivery contains stools imported from another country. How can the shopkeeper handle the change fairly?
questions.answer: Keep the advertisement because the price is unchanged.
options: Omit where every stool was made and leave the existing advertisement in place.
Label the imported stools accurately and update the advertisement.
Keep the advertisement because the price is unchanged.
Advertise the imported stools as local because they are sold in the same town.
questions.explanation: Selling a product locally does not establish where it was made. Accurate labels let buyers make an informed decision.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Apply responsibility and honesty in making and selling goods.
questions.prompt: A customer asks a weaver to deliver a large order by Wednesday. The weaver knows it cannot be finished before Friday. What is the responsible response?
questions.answer: Accept the order and wait until Wednesday to explain the delay.
options: Promise Wednesday and instruct the team to skip the final quality check.
Take the payment and ask the customer to choose a different product later.
Explain the earliest realistic delivery date before accepting the order.
Accept the order and wait until Wednesday to explain the delay.
questions.explanation: An honest deadline lets the customer decide whether to proceed and avoids pressure to rush workmanship.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify disputes between countries and assess cooperative responses that consider both sides.
questions.prompt: Which example shows a disagreement between countries rather than a disagreement within one country?
questions.answer: Two neighbouring countries dispute where their shared border runs.
options: Two neighbouring countries dispute where their shared border runs.
Two classes disagree over the results of a quiz.
Two traders in the same market argue about a stall.
Two schools in one town request the same sports ground.
questions.explanation: An international conflict is a dispute between countries. A disagreement about a border between two countries fits that description.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify disputes between countries and assess cooperative responses that consider both sides.
questions.prompt: Two countries draw different maps of the same boundary. They agree to meet with a neutral organisation. What can the organisation do to help them work towards a solution?
questions.answer: Publish only the map of the larger country.
options: Help both countries share their evidence and discuss possible agreements.
Publish only the map of the larger country.
Require the country farther away to withdraw its evidence.
Cancel the meeting until both countries already agree.
questions.explanation: An impartial meeting helps each side understand the other's position and gives them a chance to work out a peaceful agreement.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify disputes between countries and assess cooperative responses that consider both sides.
questions.prompt: A river flows through two countries. After a dry season, the country upstream plans to use more water. The country downstream says its farmers are already short of water. Which plan best considers both countries' needs?
questions.answer: Give all water to the country whose farms are larger.
options: Require the downstream farmers to choose new crops without discussion.
Share river measurements and agree how both countries will reduce use when flows are low.
Give all water to the country whose farms are larger.
Keep the river measurements private and let both countries take as much as they want.
questions.explanation: Shared measurements establish what water is available. An agreed shortage plan lets both countries prepare and share the burden.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify disputes between countries and assess cooperative responses that consider both sides.
questions.prompt: Two countries agree to reopen a crossing after a dispute about cargo checks. Travellers still wait for hours because each country gives drivers different instructions. Which joint step would address that difficulty?
questions.answer: Hold a celebration at the crossing without changing the instructions.
options: Ask drivers to check which official is on duty before loading.
Reduce opening hours while keeping the separate instructions.
Agree on one clear checklist and publish it on both sides of the border.
Hold a celebration at the crossing without changing the instructions.
questions.explanation: A common checklist resolves the immediate cause of many delays by giving drivers the same requirements on both sides.
